issue_context.title: Enable newly added entities, under system options is ignored
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Although I disabled the option ‘Enable newly added entities’. under system options, newly registered devices are automatically added as enabled entities (should be disabled). Very annoying. Have to disable entities on a daily base.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

Core-2022.2.9

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Core-2021.12.10

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Fritz

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fritz/

> just to be sure -...

Hi
There is also an associated device. Example:

``ESP-FC5300 Internet Access``

I think that, since 2022.2, the name of new devices is extended with 'Internet Access' Older devices didn't have that name extension.

This example device has two entities:
A disabled switch entity: ``ESP-FC5300 Internet Access``
An initially enabled device_ tracker: ``ESP-FC5300``

I think the device name should not have the same extended name of the switch entity
The tracker should be disabled, just like the switch

>

- New Device: iPad Internet Access
- and the device_tracker: iPad

Thx for the update😊

In have just one 5490 Fritz device that is the router. Behind the router, on the LAN Ports I have two netgear switches and six asus RTN66u devices configured as AP's.
So no mesh, old discovery method. 
When new devices connect my network (typically mobiles), a device is created with a disabled switch and an enabled device tracker. 
Since the last update, the device name is indeed not extended anymore, so that aspect is fixed!
The original issue remains: the setting 'Enable newly added entities.' is still ignored for the device trackers.

> The original issue remains: the setting 'Enable newly added entities.' is still ignored for the device trackers.

This is the newly intended behavior, that new device_trackers only by enabled, if there is already an correspondig device created by another integration - see [Improved handling of device tracker entities](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2022/02/02/release-20222/#improved-handling-of-device-tracker-entities) from release notes of 2022.2

Edit: after I'm writing this, I see that you have the issue, even when "Enable newly added entities" is disabled, newly devices were added 🤔

> This is the newly intended behavior, that new device_trackers only by enabled, if there is already an correspondig device created by another integration - see [Improved handling of device tracker entities](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2022/02/02/release-20222/#improved-handling-of-device-tracker-entities) from release notes of 2022.2

This is not related, there are no corresponding devices involved. It's about the setting that is ignored

Hi @erkr 

please enable following debug logging, restart HA and provide the homeassistant.log after a new device is created, even "Enable newly added entities." is disabled
To do so add the following to your `configuration.yaml`:
```yaml
logger:
  default: info
  logs:
    homeassistant.components.fritz: debug
    homeassistant.helpers.entity_platform: debug
    homeassistant.helpers.entity_registry: debug
```

Note: it is better to drag the log into the comment (_which will add it as an attachment_) and not copy paste as it is hard to read logs in GitHub.

review_comments: I have a bit mixed feelings on this fix. On one hand I really want to remove this feature. It's no longer necessary with the current approach of only creating entities for devices that are integrated in Home Assistant. On the other hand, it's a bug and removal can happen at another time with a deprecation period.

in case of the `fritz` integration it is a bit more complex, since the integration creates a switch entity for each discovered client in network (_to control "internet access" policy_), which has `device_info`, those creates a device by its own.
Maybe we should extend the approach "of only creating entities for devices that are integrated", that the origin domain/integration of the device_tracker is ignored? 🤔
Oh it would be nice if you could adopt the same approach as we have for device trackers to switch entities or any other type.
I think if an new entity is enabled or disabled, should be controlled by the users choice of "Enable newly added entities.", or am I wrong  🤔
That feature wouldn't exist if we remove it 🙃
